![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/ce36be89987c16762ad2b2e21d38cf78ec565f0aada219c982da6ea5eb958c1c.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2x$ for $z\ge 0,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $1$ centered at $(1,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =2x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/31a18ebb9608ff60a4a5ecbcfa8defcb6a64337b126cb5859cb042f1019b1194.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{3\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\sqrt{({\rho }^{2})^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{3z}{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ[\rho ]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-0)\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & =2\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,d\theta  \\  & =2\cdot [-{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =2\cdot [{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =2\cdot (1-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
